findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee turn off the faucet after properly hand washing without using a barrier. CORRECTED- Education was provided regarding the need for a barrier, and the employee re-washed hands appropriately. Ensure all employees are properly educated and reminded about proper hand washing procedures. The lack of a barrier allows clean hands to be re-contaminated.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the kitchen sanitizer bucket (of quaternary ammonia) to be testing below the proper sanitizing concentration (100 ppm). CORRECTED- employee remade sanitizer bucket at a concentration of 400 ppm. Ensure sanitizer is made (and tested) at a frequency to hold the proper sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacterer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Foods in the countertop cooler were observed above 41F. Hard boiled eggs were observed at 48.5F, American cheese was observed at 45.5F, ham was observed at 49.5, cream cheese was observed at 60.5F and 58.5F, all probed. The person in charge (PIC) stated that the all items with the exception of one packet of ham had been in the cooler for over 4 hours. CORRECTED- the items that had been in the temperature danger zone for over 4 hours were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. The packaging for the cream cheese, ham, and american cheese were labeled “refrigerate after opening.” The ham that had been in the cooler for 2 hours was moved to the working prep cooler to quickly cool to 41F or below. Ensure TCS foods are held at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: The countertop cooler is not holding foods at 41F or below. Multiple TCS foods were discarded as a results (see violation #22). Discussed monitoring temperatures with probe thermometer and moving TCS foods to the nearby prep cooler that is holding foods at 41F or below. Inspector will return on 1/26/26 to ensure the cold holding unit has either been serviced or replaced, OR being used to only hold non-TCS foods (cooling for quality as opposed to food safety).
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed facility’s probe thermometer to be registering 8F over correct value. CORRECTED- inspector provided education on calibrating stem thermometers using the ice water method, and re-calibrated thermometer. Ensure all food temperature measure devices are kept in correct calibration to ensure proper hot and cold holding temperatures for TCS foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple wet sanitizer cloths being stored on the kitchen counter. CORRECTED- education was provided about proper storage of wet sanitizing cloths. Ensure sanitizing cloths are stored in a sanitizing solution in between uses to prevent the growth and harborage of mold and bacteria with high water activity.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed clam shells containers being stored on the floor in dry storage. CORRECTED- inspector discussed violation with the PIC, who moved the containers off of the ground. Ensure all single service container are stored at least 6” above the ground to prevent the contamination of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.[C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: A carton of raw shell eggs was observed on the top shelf of the 2 door cooler, above bread, cream cheese, and salad dressing. CORRECTED- PIC removed the eggs and voluntarily discarded them. The eggs were delivered by accident and are not used in the facility. Ensure raw shell eggs are stored below ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Foods in the countertop cooler were observed above 41F. Salsa portions were observed at 48F, sliced cheese at 50F, veggie sausage at 54F, and deli ham at 52F, all probed. PIC stated that the sliced cheese, veggie sausage, and ham were stocked in the cooler about 30 minutes prior to initial checks. Temperatures had not changed 30 minutes later, 1 hour after foods were placed in the cooler. CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were moved to a functional cooler to quickly cool to 41F or below. Ensure TCS foods are held at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: A spray bottle of Clorox Scentiva disinfectant was observed stored on the countertop in the back kitchen area, where food is prepared. CORRECTED- The spray bottle was moved to storage away from food prep surfaces. The disinfectant is used on the cash register countertop, not for food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The countertop cooler is not holding foods at 41F or below. Salsa portions were observed at 48F, sliced cheese at 50F, veggie sausage at 54F, and deli ham at 52F, all probed. Discussed turning down the cooler temperature or moving TCS foods to the nearby prep cooler that is holding foods at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: An ice scoop in the small ice bin was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. Discussed proper storage with staff and PIC. Store ice scoops so that the handle does not touch the ice, and the scoop can be used without touching the ice.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: No prepared sanitizer bucket was available during this inspection. CORRECTED- Upon request, a sanitizer bucket was prepared. Ensure sanitizer buckets are prepared before beginning to engage in food prep, and refreshed as needed throughout the day.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: There is a bare wood 2x4 on the wall holding a syrups rack on the wall. Paint or otherwise seal the bare wood so it is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No CFM was present when inspector arrived to begin this inspection. PIC/owner arrived as inspector was sitting down to write the report. Seven employees are scheduled to take the CFM course later this month, and owner indicated that another 6-8 are interested as well. Ensure sufficient staff have CFM certificates to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee entered the food prep area and donned gloves without washing hands first. Inspector discussed with owners, who will educate staff on handwashing.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw eggs observed stored above danish filling and ready-to-eat bacon in the 2 door cooler. CORRECTED- Storage rearranged to store eggs below ready-to-eat foods.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. Upon request, an employee demonstrated how they get sanitizer from the wall mounted dispenser. Staff had diluted the sanitizer after it was dispensed from the wall mounted dispenser. As dispensed (prior to employee’s dilution) sanitizer was observed at 300ppm quat. CORRECTED- Sanitizer bucket was remade. Discussed sanitizer bucket preparation with employee.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Two damp wiping cloths observed stored on the counters in the barista area and in the food prep area. Store wet wiping cloths submerged in sanitizer between uses.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Ice scoops in all ice bins observed stored with handles touching the ice. Discussed proper storage practices with staff. Store ice scoops with the handle sticking out so that the handle doesn’t touch the ice, and the scoop can be used without touching the ice.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container; (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Bare wood observed exposed in two locations: 1) under the barista counter dipping well; and 2) at the ends of the countertop that the toasters sit on. Seal bare wood so it is smooth, easily cleanable, and no longer absorbent.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
Both restroom doors are not self-closing. Add self-closers to the restroom doors.
6-202.14: Toilet rooms located on PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with tightfitting and self-closing door. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
